title: fix: stabilize Docker build context, Prisma runtime, and automated schema migration
body:
- [x] Create `.dockerignore` to exclude node_modules and other artifacts from build context
- [x] Harden `Dockerfile` (Alpine + OpenSSL, fix Prisma runtime artifacts ownership, fix entrypoint permissions)
- [x] Fix `docker-entrypoint.sh` to use bundled Prisma binary directly (no npx, no permission issues)
- [x] Update `docker-compose.yml` (remove obsolete `version`, improve DB healthcheck, add schema in DATABASE_URL, explicit build section)
- [x] Pin Prisma version to `5.22.0` in `package.json` (matches lock file exactly)
- [x] Update `README.md` with comprehensive operational docs in Spanish (fresh start, rebuild, normal up, troubleshooting)
- [x] Remove `docker-compose*.yml` from `.dockerignore` (avoids confusion in future builds)
- [x] Remove insecure `JWT_SECRET` fallback in `docker-compose.yml` (prevents weak-secret deploys)

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Create a single comprehensive pull request in repository `dragonhack991-crypto/iapos` based on branch `copilot/setup-initial-pos-system` that stabilizes Dockerized production/runtime behavior, Prisma schema deployment, and operational reliability for setup/login flows.

Context from user-reported failures:
- Docker build fails with: `invalid file request node_modules/.bin/.acorn-*` due to bad build context.
- Runtime Prisma commands pulled Prisma 7 via npx, conflicting with Prisma 5 schema expectations (`P1012` about datasource url).
- Missing runtime Prisma artifacts caused `Cannot find module '/app/node_modules/@prisma/client/generator-build/index.js'`.
- Compose warning about obsolete `version` key.
- Migration service had EACCES when npx tried writing under `/home/nextjs`.
- User ultimately got setup/login working manually but wants an automatic, robust solution.

Goals for this PR (single large PR):
1) Docker build context and image reliability
- Add/fix `.dockerignore` to exclude `node_modules`, nested node_modules, `.next`, `.git`, env files, logs, build artifacts, etc.
- Ensure Docker build no longer sends host `node_modules` and avoids invalid file request errors.

2) Dockerfile hardening for Next.js standalone + Prisma
- Keep multi-stage build and production runner.
- Ensure OpenSSL and certs available where needed.
- Ensure runtime image contains required Prisma runtime pieces for app execution.
- Avoid requiring ad-hoc interactive installs during container runtime.
- Keep non-root app execution where practical.

3) Prisma version consistency
- Pin Prisma toolchain to a compatible version in project manifests (e.g., `prisma` and `@prisma/client` aligned; no floating major upgrades that cause Prisma 7 behavior unexpectedly).
- Update lockfile as needed.

4) Automatic schema sync/migration path in compose startup
- Make `docker compose up --build` work end-to-end without manual intervention.
- Implement a robust strategy to apply schema changes automatically before app serves traffic (either dedicated migrate service or app entrypoint flow), avoiding permission errors and interactive prompts.
- If using npx at runtime, make it non-interactive and permission-safe.
- Ensure app depends on successful migration/sync.

5) Compose cleanup and health
- Remove obsolete `version` usage.
- Keep DB healthcheck and correct app dependency ordering.
- Ensure logs are clear and startup behavior deterministic.

6) Operational docs
- Update README (or relevant docs) with exact commands for:
  - fresh start
  - rebuild
  - normal up
  - troubleshooting quick checks
- Include explicit note about fixed Prisma version and automated schema step.

Acceptance criteria:
- `docker compose build --no-cache app` succeeds without node_modules context errors.
- `docker compose up --build` starts db, applies schema automatically, and starts app without manual Prisma commands.
- Setup and login paths remain functional.
- No interactive prompt is required during migration/sync.
- Changes are coherent and production-safe for this repo’s current architecture.

Please implement the code/config/doc changes directly and open one PR with a clear summary, testing notes, and any follow-ups.
